$license_note: autogpt_platform/ is PolyForm Shield. Railway staff ruling 2026-08-08: fine to template while a self-hosted option exists; an owner takedown request unpublishes the template, no account strike. Business risk accepted.
$topology_note: 5 services instead of upstream's 16. All ten backend processes run in one container as the same 8 per-service commands upstream compose runs, launched by boot/backend-boot.sh in one container (the `app` monolith deadlocks on Linux: fork-with-threads); every *_HOST defaults to localhost so colocation is zero-config, and the workspace volume (which multiple backend processes write) cannot be shared across Railway services anyway. clamav is skipped via CLAMAV_SERVICE_ENABLED=false (official flag, default true). falkordb/graphiti is skipped: rollout is gated on a LaunchDarkly flag self-host deploys never see.

postgres.$note: Upstream compose uses this exact image; the app needs the vector extension so Railway's own postgres template won't do. PGDATA subdir dodges the lost+found initdb refusal (gotchas.md).

redis.$note: The backend cache client is cluster-only (backend/data/redis_client.py imports RedisCluster exclusively), so a plain redis fails. Single node in cluster mode owning all 16384 slots satisfies it. Upstream treats cache as disposable and explicitly warns persisting nodes.conf pins stale peers, so: no volume, config file in /tmp. announce-hostname uses the private domain so CLUSTER SLOTS hands clients a resolvable name. protected-mode off is safe on the private network and required because cluster clients redirect between announced addresses.
redis.startCommand: /bin/sh -c "redis-server --port 6379 --cluster-enabled yes --cluster-config-file /tmp/nodes.conf --cluster-require-full-coverage no --cluster-announce-hostname $RAILWAY_PRIVATE_DOMAIN --cluster-preferred-endpoint-type hostname --protected-mode no & until redis-cli -p 6379 ping >/dev/null 2>&1; do sleep 1; done; redis-cli -p 6379 cluster addslotsrange 0 16383 || true; wait"

rabbitmq.$note: Version pinned to upstream compose. Backend reads RABBITMQ_DEFAULT_USER/PASS names directly.

backend.$note: Overlay image: caddy muxes REST (8006) and websocket (8001) onto one $PORT because a Railway domain targets a single port and the template config rejects targetPort keys (memory: railway-template-config-limits). Boot runs prisma migrate deploy with retry (no init containers on Railway), then launches the 8 upstream service commands under a shell supervisor. Healthcheck /health is served by the REST app at root, NOT /api/health.

variables.$JWT_JWKS_URL_note: public https, not private http: the auth lib refuses cleartext JWKS from any dotted hostname (autogpt_libs/auth/config.py) and Railway private domains are dotted. https skips that check entirely.
variables.$ENCRYPTION_KEY_note: hex alphabet because fernet needs base64 which secret() cannot emit; boot script derives the fernet key from the hex (SparkyFitness precedent for the alphabet arg).

frontend.$note: Overlay image: sentinel URLs baked into the Next.js client bundle at CI build get sed-rewritten to these runtime values at boot. Better Auth is embedded in this server and talks to postgres directly; its tables live in the platform schema created by backend migrations, so first boot may 500 on auth routes until backend migrations finish - restart policy rides it out.

variables.$AGPT_SERVER_URL_note: server-side reads go over the public URL rather than private :8006 because the REST bind interface on v6 private is unverified; revisit if egress cost matters.

$deployer_prompts: None required. LLM provider keys are added inside the app per-user (Settings > Credentials), so the template deploys with zero prompts.
$source_project_note: In the LIVE source project, cross-service RAILWAY_PUBLIC_DOMAIN references resolve EMPTY (memory: railway-cross-service-public-domain); set those five URL vars as literals there and only use the reference form in the repaired template config.
